summary: Iter63 — regression verification of the code-quality refactor (circular-import split, sessionStorage migration, stable BlockPreview keys). All checks pass. Backend: 17/17 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_iter63_refactor_regression.py (both import orders resolve cleanly, /api/health 200, GET /apps/{id}/locks shape correct, master toggle flips state, granular toggle works for every one of the 9 supported kinds (page, block, form, cms_collection, cms_item, workflow, data_destination, app_mode, overview), invalid kind rejected with 400, client editor gets 423 on PATCH /apps/{id}/pages/{page_id} against a locked page, owner passes, edit-request lands in inbox, admin approve issues a single-use grant, editor's next save succeeds, and the very next save is blocked again with 423 proving consume_grant is wired through the shared module). Frontend evidence via page.evaluate on the live preview URL: legacy localStorage['site_admin_token_pv_e72ca0b15cbe1463cd72e2fa'] is migrated to sessionStorage and localStorage is emptied on reload; likewise for site_member_token_<token>; no token key remains under Object.keys(localStorage) after migration. BlockPreview: all 4 pages of tenant Formcheck Medical (Home/About/Services/Contact) plus the 16-design template gallery render with ZERO 'Each child in a list should have a unique key' warnings and ZERO ReferenceErrors (checked via page.on('console') and page.on('pageerror')). The only 2 console errors seen are unrelated 401s on protected endpoints when browsing signed-out. lock_shared.py cleanly owns KINDS/LABELS/active_grant/consume_grant; locks.py and edit_requests.py both import it at module top and neither imports the other.
critical_code_review_comments: lock_shared.py is a clean one-directional cut: locks.py and edit_requests.py both import from it at module top; the previous deferred function-level `from edit_requests import ...` / `from locks import ...` calls are gone. `python3 -c 'import locks; import edit_requests'` works in either order.

edit_requests.py:288 still has a function-level `from edit_requests import consume_grant` inside studio.py's update_page — actually studio.py:288 imports consume_grant lazily. That deferred import is fine for now (studio.py is not part of the cycle) but could be lifted to a module-top `from lock_shared import consume_grant` for consistency.

The lock 423 enforcement lives only on the multi-page endpoint PATCH /apps/{id}/pages/{page_id} (via page_guard.assert_can_edit_page + locks.blocked_block_edits). The legacy PUT /apps/{id}/page in server.py:624 has NO lock check and would let any editor bypass locks by hitting that older route. Not touched by this refactor, but worth flagging — the endpoint is still routed and returns 200 with `{ok:true,count:N}` even when the target page is locked. Recommend either deleting the legacy endpoint or adding the same assert_can_edit_page guard.

SiteAdmin.jsx + MemberGate.jsx migration is idempotent and safe: readSiteJwt/readJwt only copy-then-delete when a legacy key is present, so repeated reloads don't churn. Verified via page.evaluate that Object.keys(localStorage) contains no token-shaped key after migration.
BlockPreview.jsx stable-key change is regression-clean across every block type used by the Formcheck Medical tenant + all 16 gallery designs — no warnings, no ReferenceErrors.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (0 key warnings, 0 ReferenceErrors, 0 pageerrors across 4 tenant pages + 16-template gallery; sessionStorage migration verified end-to-end)
